x: A hands-on guide that teaches Process GPT step by step from scratch: describe a company's routine work in words to turn it into a process, teach AI agent colleagues the company's documents, and attach business rules as decision tables. What is Process GPT Process GPT is an open-source platform for business processes and AI agents together . The order of the work and who does each part are defined in BPMN, the international standard notation, and each step is done by a person or handed to an AI agent. You don't need to know how to draw BPMN. Describe the work you want in the chat, and Process GPT creates the flow diagram and the input forms. This tutorial follows the story of Hanbit Office , an office furniture company. Character Role Jinyoung Jang Sales team lead. The person you play in this tutorial, and the Process GPT admin Minji Kim Sales representative. Takes customer requests and writes proposals Seoyeon Park Finance officer. Approves high-value quotes Hanbit Office Quote Advisor An AI colleague that reads the price list and writes draft quotes (you build it in Chapter 9) Getting started — Install Process GPT and look around the screens. Process basics — Describe the "Sales Proposal Creation" work in chat to turn it into a process, look inside the resulting definition (flow diagram, roles, forms), and manage its versions. AI agents — Upload the product price list to the Knowledge Base so answers are based on it, then build an agent colleague that writes draft quotes and chat with it. Use the quote approval policy to create a process that includes agents. Tools and rules — Turn the volume discount criteria into a decision table (DMN) through chat and attach it to an agent. Operations — Bring in colleagues and change the display language and settings. Learning path Getting started Install, first sign-in, look around the screens Process basics Create a process through chat, look inside the definition, versions AI agents Knowledge Base, building and chatting with agent colleagues, processes from documents Tools and rules Decision tables (DMN) made through chat Operations Colleague sign-up, language, settings Each chapter goes Why → Try it → Check your understanding . Later chapters build on what you made in earlier ones, so it's best to follow them in order. The answers to the check questions are folded away — try them yourself first, then open them. Chapters coming soon Chapters marked "Coming soon" in the table of contents on the left (Skills, Run the steps agents handle, Connect external tools with MCP, Execution analytics, Strategy board, Final project) will be published one by one after fixes now underway in the current version are in. Chapter numbers are fixed in advance, so they won't change when these chapters appear. Who this tutorial is for If you've worked with email and a messenger, you can follow along. No programming needed. For the installation (Chapter 1), you only need to paste a few commands into a terminal. You don't need to know BPMN. Each chapter explains as much as you need. What you need Item Details Computer macOS, Linux or Windows (WSL2) that runs Docker. 16 GB of memory or more and 70 GB of free disk space recommended LLM key One OpenAI API key Practice files Hanbit Office sales docs (zip) — the product price list ( Hanbit-Office-Price-List.pdf ) and the bulk order quote approval policy ( Hanbit-Office-Quote-Approval-Policy.pdf ) (Chapters 8 and 12) The screens in this tutorial All screens and results in this tutorial come from a fresh Process GPT install made as in Chapter 1 and actually run. The text and flows the AI produces vary a little each run, so it's fine if the words on your screen don't exactly match the pictures. What matters is that the items listed under What to check in each chapter are there.

x: Hanbit Office team lead Jinyoung Jang describes the sales proposal work in chat. Process GPT shows a draft with the steps, owners and flow, gets your confirmation, then creates and saves a process definition with a BPMN flow diagram and input forms. Why make it a process Whenever a customer asks for a proposal, the Hanbit Office sales team works in the same order. They take down what the customer asks for, and a sales representative reads it, writes the proposal and sends it. Today this goes back and forth by email and messenger, so you have to ask to find out how far a request has got, and when the person in charge changes, the notes sometimes get lost. Turning this order into a process changes things like this. Case by case As a process People remember who does what next The steps and owners are written in the definition Notes are scattered across email and messenger They stay in the input form set for each step You have to ask to know the progress The progress of each case (instance) is visible on screen Process GPT stores processes as BPMN . BPMN is the international standard notation that draws a workflow as steps, gateways and owner bands (lanes). You don't need to know how to draw it. Describe it in words, and Process GPT draws it. Try it 1 — Pick an agent and describe the work In the chat box on the home screen (the pencil icon at the top of the sidebar), click Deep Agent ▾ and switch to Basic Agent . Picking an agent — Basic Agent, Deep Agent, Codex Why Basic Agent Deep Agent can also create processes, and it builds skills and agents along with them. But it takes several minutes because it works through many steps on its own, and in the current version it sometimes ends with "Something went wrong while putting the process files together, so I'm holding the result back." While you're learning, we recommend the short and reliable Basic Agent . Describe the process you want in the chat box. Say who does what at each step, and say that you need forms. Basic Agent selected and the description typed in Try it 2 — Review the draft When you send it, a new chat room opens and a draft appears within a few seconds (about 8 seconds in our run). Its title is "Shall I create the process from this draft?". It lists the process name, the steps and the role that owns each one, the flow, and open questions. The draft — process name “Sales Proposal Creation”, steps 1. [Customer] Submit request · 2. [Sales Representative] Write and send proposal, the flow, and open questions (None) What to check : two steps with their owners (Customer, Sales Representative) and a flow from the customer to the sales representative to the end ("Customer(Submit request) → Sales Representative(Write and send proposal) → End" in our run). The wording differs a little each run. Below the draft are options. Option What it does Create the process as is Creates the process from this draft Break the steps down further · Make it more concise · Adjust the roles Revises the draft and shows it again Write your own (optional) Type the change yourself. Example: Have the sales representative take down the request instead of the customer Choose "Create the process as is", then click Submit response . Choosing alone doesn't send anything. Just before clicking “Submit response” with “Create the process as is” chosen Try it 3 — Confirm it was created After you submit, "Selected: Create the process as is" and then "Created a work item to generate the process from the consultation." appear. Soon "✅ BPMN process generation complete — 1 process has been created. The process definition has been saved. You can find it in the left menu." arrives. In our run, it took about 24 seconds from sending the description to the saved definition. Below the message is the BPMN process generation result card ( Saved , plus the process name "Sales Proposal Creation" and its ID). A process created by Basic Agent is saved without you saving it separately. In other runs it took about 15–25 seconds

Then ask Hanbit Office Quote Advisor , which has the rule attached, and it answers with the discount rate from that rule. Why a decision table When a rule like “20–49 of the same product get 5%, 50–99 get 8% …” sits in a document as text, people and AI have to reread and interpret it every time. A decision table puts such rules into rows of “condition (When) → result (Then)”. The standard name is DMN (Decision Model and Notation), and Process GPT calls it a business rule . Rule written as text Decision table Each reader may interpret it differently Each condition has exactly one result row Hard to find what changed after an edit Saved as versions you can compare The agent has to find and read the document The agent finds the rule and uses it directly Try it 1 — Make a decision table by describing it Under Agent Colleagues in the sidebar, open Hanbit Office Quote Advisor ( Chapter 10 ). Problems we actually ran into while making this tutorial, and how to fix them. Follow the chapter numbers for details. Installing and signing in http://localhost:8088 doesn't open. Check that the launcher ran to the end. The first run takes a while because it downloads the images. Use docker compose ps to check that nginx is up; if it isn't, run ./start-all-services.sh … once more. If another program is using port 8088, close that program ( Chapter 1 ). When I sign up, it says “Invalid email format”. There must be a dot after the @ . Write it like jinyoung@hanbit.example . A local install doesn't send email, so it doesn't have to be a real address ( Chapter 1 ). The colleague who signed up second isn't an admin. That's expected. Only the first person to sign up is an admin; everyone after that joins as a regular user ( Chapter 18 ). I sent a chat message and Deep Agent says its sandbox isn't available. Deep Agent couldn't start its work container. Create the docker-compose.override.yml from Chapter 1 and start the services again. I want to start over. Run ./stop-all-services.sh --wipe , then run the launcher again. All data (accounts, processes, documents) is deleted. Chat and processes I sent the same sentence, but the diagram and answer are different. Text and flows made by AI differ a little on every run. It's fine as long as each chapter's What to check (step names, amounts, rules and so on) matches. I see “unknown” in the process hierarchy on the version comparison screen. It's a display issue in the current version. Expand Uncategorized › unknown › Uncategorized all the way down and pick the process ( Chapter 4 ). I renamed a step, but it's back to the old name when I reopen it. The 💾 in the step panel only updates the flow diagram. Save the definition with the 💾 at the top right of the definition screen to create a version ( Chapter 4 ). Deep Agent says “Something went wrong while putting the process files together, so I'm holding the result back.” The definition Deep Agent made didn't pass validation yet. Reply in the same chat room, for example "Yes, please create the process with this flow." (or "Yes, please fix it that way." when you asked for a fix), and it tries again. In our run, it reported the fix after one reply. If it keeps happening, start a new chat with a more specific request (steps, owners and gateways) ( Chapter 12 ).
